sophie: quick follow-up to pinning rfc - thinking of 'sparse lease' tokens to reduce rollout metadata size for very large tenants. leases become small opaque ids with ttl and tiny hints, not full model refs. @rahul @jamie thoughts?

rahul: huge win for storage. how do clients handle unknown lease ids?

sophie: plan: servers accept old pins and new leases. unknown lease id => client calls /resolve-lease endpoint (non-blocking recommended). resolver returns resolution or 404. treat as soft miss.

jamie: need compat phases: (1) accept+telemetry, (2) server resolution cache + background backfill, (3) deprecate embedded pins after 6mo. clients must be non-blocking in hot paths.

rahul: SDK will ship resolveLease helper to populate local cache asynchronously. fallback to primary model if unresolved.

tess: telemetry: tag requests that triggered resolution, emit resolution latency histograms, and count lease->model-change events. dashboards + alerts.

sophie: token fields: lease_kind enum {full,sparse,ephemeral}, lease_id (hmac), ttl_seconds, affinity optional, small hints. include compat_version integer.

jamie: server: LRU+TTL resolution cache, lazy fetch queue, migration job to move heavy tenants gradually. feature flag per-tenant use_sparse_lease.

rahul: security: lease_id must be HMAC/KMS-signed, non-guessable. redact tenant ids from telemetry or hash them.

sophie: edge-case: lease resolves to new model mid-session. return resolved_model_id + resolved_at so client can decide to stick. default stickiness = min(ttl,300s).

tess: rollout: 1% canary for internal tenant 48h. fail if miss_rate >1% or p95>200ms. emit lease_migration tags: created/resolved/evicted/expired/renewed.

ops-bot: deploybot: created canary internal-canary-3 with use_sparse_lease=true at 2026-03-23T15:12:00Z :rocket: 

jamie: ops playbook: on resolution flood auto-scale resolver, circuit-break to full pins, alert; add alert for lease churn.

sophie: I'll draft server resolver doc with HMAC format and migration checklist. rahul to draft SDK adapter, tess to write metrics dashboard. thanks all :thumbsup:
